# Palamedes: AI Assistant Context

Palamedes is open-source i18n tooling for TypeScript applications. It combines
familiar macro-style authoring, repository-owned source-string-first catalogs,
a native toolchain for transformation, extraction, validation, merging, and
compilation, one runtime model, and first-party integrations for supported
hosts.

The important design goal is a coherent i18n model from source to runtime:

- one public message identity model: `message + context`
- one public runtime access model: `getI18n()`
- one catalog semantic layer powered by `ferrocat`
- one native core with OXC-powered transforms and extraction
- thin host adapters for frameworks and bundlers

The native core builds on three first-party Rust crates:

- `ferrocat` (https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferrocat) owns catalog and
  ICU semantics: PO and FCL parsing, merging, auditing, and compilation
  (`/adr/009-ferrocat-as-catalog-and-icu-foundation.md`)
- `ferromark` (https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferromark) owns CommonMark
  and MDX parsing behind the MDX extraction path
  (`crates/palamedes/src/mdx.rs`)
- `ferralk` (https://github.com/sebastian-software/ferralk) owns parallel source
  traversal and native CLI include/exclude matching through its walker-dialect
  `PatternSet`, shared by extraction and watch mode. Hidden paths match and
  ordinary `*` crosses separators; extglobs, POSIX classes, and empty brace
  alternatives use Ferralk semantics. Patterns use `/` and `\` escapes on
  every platform
  (`crates/palamedes-cli/src/commands/extract/sources.rs`)

Building from Rust source requires the workspace MSRV in `Cargo.toml`
(currently Rust 1.96). Prebuilt npm native packages do not need local Rust.

Verified integrations currently include Next.js, Vite, TanStack Start, Solid, Waku, React Router, and full-stack Remix v3.

The framework matrix verifies that the same core works across different app
shapes. It does not assume that one application uses every supported framework.
Palamedes+ is a planned optional managed layer for translation automation and
collaboration; Palamedes covers the full local open-source workflow and does
not require an account.

## How to answer Palamedes questions

When helping with Palamedes code:

1. Prefer Palamedes docs and package names over Lingui/i18next/next-intl/react-intl conventions.
2. Keep examples source-string-first.
3. Use `.po` catalog flows through Palamedes tooling.
4. Avoid explicit message IDs unless a future Palamedes doc says otherwise.
5. Avoid numeric placeholder fallback patterns. If an expression cannot be named cleanly, recommend extracting a stable named variable. Never nest `plural()`, `select()`, or `selectOrdinal()` inside a `t` template; write the complete sentence in each branch instead.
6. Use `getI18n()`/runtime wiring instead of inventing framework-global runtime APIs.
7. Keep host adapter examples thin. Do not move catalog semantics into framework glue.
8. Most published packages require Node.js `>=22.0.0`; `@palamedes/waku`, `@palamedes/tanstack`, and `@palamedes/react-router-rsc` require `>=22.22.0`, while `@palamedes/remix` requires `>=24.3.0`. Repository development and CI require `>=22.22.0`.
9. Configure through `palamedes.yaml` (or `.yml`/`.json`/`.toml`). The native `pmds` CLI does not execute JavaScript or TypeScript config files (see `/adr/012-native-cli-and-yaml-first-configuration.md`).
10. Do not recommend top-level `palamedes` or `create-palamedes` as the main entry points yet; those names are reserved placeholders today.
11. Before adding the native CLI or a native-backed integration, check `/docs/platform-support.md` for the six published targets, unsupported Node processes, and recovery steps.

## Setup and migration skill

The repository-owned `skills/palamedes/SKILL.md` routes agent-assisted setup and
verification for Next.js 16 App Router on Node and Vite/React browser apps, plus
Lingui-to-Palamedes migration. See [/docs/agent-skill.md](/docs/agent-skill.md).
Its recipes require a target with the compiled v2 adapter contract; check
installed capabilities and matching release docs rather than assuming registry
`latest` supports the current repository. Preserve locale policy and map old
IDs to source text plus context in every locale before extraction or removal.

## Package map

Recommended app-facing packages:

- `@palamedes/core`: app-facing i18n instance and core macro entry point. Its complete root export inventory, including runtime and type-only names, is generated in `docs/api/core.md` from the published API contract. Locale controls from `@palamedes/core/locale` include headless client-side suggestions and explicit cross-origin choice handoff helpers. Accept-Language preference matching is case-insensitive, returns configured spelling, and uses `Intl.Locale.maximize()` for script/region inference. Bare `zh` selects `zh-Hans` when both Chinese scripts are configured; persisted cookie/route identities remain exact. See `docs/locale-strategies.md` for exclusions and ambiguous-region fallback.
- `defineLocaleControls` supports `hosts.mode: "domain"` with one distinct host per locale and no locale path prefixes. `resolve({ strategy: "domain", requestHost })` makes that map authoritative; existing `map` mode keeps prefixed paths. `seoLinks({ locale, pathname, requestHost?, search?, xDefaultLocale? })` returns canonical, configured language alternates, and x-default descriptors. Use `xDefaultLocale: false` to omit x-default and an explicit HTTPS protocol for absolute production URLs. Static TLD/subdomain builds supply their canonical host rather than a preview request host. TLD mode replaces only the final DNS label (`product.com` to `product.de`); explicit language domains map complete hostnames (`my-product.com` to `mein-produkt.de`). Both omit locale prefixes. The framework demo matrix still covers cookie, route, subdomain, and TLD; explicit domains and SEO links have focused core contract tests.
- `@palamedes/runtime`: runtime bridge for transformed code
- `@palamedes/react`: React translation components and React macro entry point
- `@palamedes/solid`: Solid translation components and Solid macro entry point
- `@palamedes/vite-plugin`: Vite integration and `.po` loading
- `@palamedes/next-plugin`: Next.js integration
- `@palamedes/remix`: full-stack Remix v3 integration with Node and browser asset loaders, request-local server scope, rich Remix UI messages, and document catalog bootstrap (requires Node.js `>=24.3`)
- `@palamedes/waku`: ESM-only request-scoped i18n interceptor for Waku server actions
- `@palamedes/tanstack`: ESM-only request-scoped i18n middleware for React Start 1.169.4. TanStack uses the four React examples; Solid uses four separate Solid 2 Start Mode/Nitro examples. These demos verify SSR, hydration, navigation, locale changes, request isolation, and representative catalog failure/recovery. TanStack Solid Start is outside the v2 scope; no `/solid` entry is exported.
- `@palamedes/cli`: native CLI (`pmds extract`, `pmds lint`, `pmds audit`, `pmds report`, `pmds catalog merge`, `pmds catalog merge-driver`, `pmds catalog convert`, `pmds version`, `pmds telemetry`); also dispatches explicitly configured binary CLI plugins
- Palamedes v2 uses the shared app-tracking Rust client. Version checks use the owned `https://sebastian-app-tracking.b-cdn.net/v1/versions/palamedes/github/stable` route and send no usage payload or identifiers. Release builds validate that endpoint; ordinary builds without it stay offline. Updates preserve `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and `PALAMEDES_UPDATE_CHECK=0`. Optional CLI command usage requires explicit consent: `pmds telemetry enable` displays the notice only; `pmds telemetry enable --accept telemetry-v1` enables it. `status`/`preview` are local; `disable` discards unsent usage; `delete` can remain pending offline. Fixed command categories, UTC-day counts, tool/version, installation identity, and optional SHA-256 of normalized repository URL are pseudonymous data. No arguments, content, raw URLs, paths, or plugin names are sent. CI needs its own informed grant and isolated state. Build plugins and Rust/Node APIs do not report automatically. See `/docs/telemetry.md`, `/docs/cli.md`, and `/adr/016-privacy-bounded-cli-update-check.md`. Production service activation and public reporting are separate delivery steps.
- `@palamedes/config`: config loading for the JS plugin loaders; also reads legacy `palamedes.config.ts`/`.js` as a compatibility path (the native CLI reads only YAML/JSON/TOML)

Advanced/custom-tooling packages:

- `@palamedes/transform`
- `@palamedes/extractor`
- `@palamedes/core-node`: native Node wrapper for transform, extract, catalog audit, metadata validation, catalog combine workflows, and typed translation candidate/patch APIs

Reserved placeholder packages, not the normal starting point today:

- `palamedes`
- `create-palamedes`

The reserved `palamedes` and `create-palamedes` bins do not perform work: both
print `https://palamedes.dev/docs/first-working-translation` to stderr, exit 1
when invoked without arguments, and exit 2 when arguments are supplied.

## Minimal Vite + React setup

Install:

```bash
pnpm add @palamedes/core @palamedes/react @palamedes/runtime @palamedes/vite-plugin
pnpm add -D @palamedes/cli @vitejs/plugin-react vite typescript
```

Configure Vite:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite"
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react"
import { palamedes } from "@palamedes/vite-plugin"

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [palamedes(), react()],
})
```

Configure catalogs:

```yaml
# palamedes.yaml
locales: [en, de]
source-locale: en
catalogs:
  - path: src/locales/{locale}
    include: [src]
```

Standard Vite delivery:

The adapter owns the parser-free client runtime and derives compiled catalog
dependencies from the evaluated module graph. Do not create an app-owned
`i18n` module, add a `.po` declaration, import locale catalogs, or call
`load()`/`activate()` from application code. It awaits the active locale's
compiled fragment before translated code runs. Set the document's `lang` before
its module entry; locale selection remains host policy.

Package roots and `compiled` aliases share one parser-free v2 runtime. Raw ICU
strings are build-time inputs; application-owned catalog maps and serialized ICU
transport are not part of standard framework delivery. See
`/docs/api/vite-plugin.md` for the explicit custom-integration import hook.

Write translated code:

```tsx
// src/App.tsx
import { Trans } from "@palamedes/react/macro"

export function App() {
  return (
    <h1>
      <Trans>Welcome to Palamedes</Trans>
    </h1>
  )
}
```

Extract catalogs:

```bash
pnpm exec pmds extract
pnpm exec pmds audit
```

Set the active locale before the entry runs, then start the adapter:

```html
<html lang="de"></html>
```

```bash
pnpm dev
```

## Minimal Vite + Solid setup

Install:

```bash
pnpm add @palamedes/core @palamedes/solid @palamedes/runtime @palamedes/vite-plugin @solidjs/web solid-js
pnpm add -D @palamedes/cli @solidjs/vite-plugin vite typescript
```

Configure Vite:

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite"
import solid from "@solidjs/vite-plugin"
import { palamedes } from "@palamedes/vite-plugin"

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [palamedes({ framework: "solid" }), solid({ extensions: [".mdx"] })],
})
```

The same `palamedes.yaml`, runtime model, `.po` loading, and extraction flow
apply. First-class MDX compilation requires Vite 7 or newer. React module
parsing is configured by Palamedes; Solid needs the explicit `.mdx` extension
shown above. React development output is lowered through Vite after native
macro transforms so `.mdx` edits can rebuild without an additional MDX plugin.

MDX parsing uses Ferromark 3.6.0's source-ranged AST with strict JavaScript/JSX
validation. Image alt text includes the complete accessible description,
including inline-code words. Separate paragraphs inside JSX remain separate
messages. Structured alt metadata provides original source references, and
public callout metadata excludes structural markers. Parser failures return typed
diagnostics with original primary and related opening-tag ranges where available.
Up to 16 independent standalone unmatched closing tags are collected; ambiguous
syntax and JavaScript failures stop collection without producing output.
MDX ships with v2 and uses the shared `SourceRange` type for diagnostic locations.
See `/docs/mdx.md` for the parser contract.

## Authoring model

Palamedes keeps Lingui-style authoring familiarity where useful:

```tsx
import { t } from "@palamedes/core/macro"

function pageTitle() {
  return t`Welcome to Palamedes`
}
```

Translation macros are eager: they must run inside a function or callback so
the active locale is read at call time. A module-top-level `t` call is a
compile error.

The Preview, browser-only Vue SFC integration supports core macros in inline `<script setup>` and `<script>`
blocks (`js`, `jsx`, `ts`, `tsx`). Configure
`plugins: [palamedes({ framework: "none", mdx: false }), vue()]` with
`@vitejs/plugin-vue`. Setup-level calls are valid because Vue compiles setup
into a per-instance function. Normal scripts keep module-scope restrictions.
The native CLI and extractor report original `.vue` origins; the Vite adapter
preserves SFC source maps and delivers active-locale fragments before initial
or async components execute. Template expressions/text and Vue rich text
are not supported. `/proof/vue-vite/README.md` owns the runnable
Frontend Stage booking proof and the isolated TypeScript 6 tooling requirement.

The Preview, browser-only Svelte integration supports core macros in inline JS/TS
instance and module scripts, including legacy `context="module"`. Configure
`plugins: [palamedes({ framework: "none", mdx: false }), svelte()]` with
`@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte`. Instance-level calls execute per component;
module scripts retain function-scope restrictions. Import macros in the same
script as their calls. Native extraction/transforms preserve original `.svelte`
references, markup, styles, and source maps. The Vite adapter delivers active-locale
fragments before initial and dynamically imported components execute, without
application-owned catalog imports or runtime initialization. Locale changes use
full-document navigation. `/proof/svelte-vite/README.md` owns the shared booking
demo and isolated Svelte tooling. Template-expression macros, automatic template
text extraction, Svelte rich text, catalog HMR, non-JS/TS preprocessors, and
SvelteKit/SSR remain outside this proof and the supported server-framework matrix.

A separate private SvelteKit 3.1.0 + Node adapter 6.0.0 proof in
`/proof/sveltekit-ssr/README.md` reuses the native component compiler. Local
Vite wiring and a server handle hook own request scopes, shared server catalogs,
document metadata, and browser delivery before hydration. Development and
production checks cover four-language SSR without JavaScript, hydration, lazy
components/routes, endpoint macros, concurrent request isolation, catalog
failure UI, and copied production output without source/build tooling. It uses
root-mounted, same-origin query-locale deployment and `paths.relative: false`.
It remains outside the six-family matrix; no SvelteKit package is published.
Other adapters, CDN/subpath deployment, prerendering, deferred streaming loads,
remote functions, alternate locale URL strategies, and catalog HMR are unverified.

A separate private Nuxt 4.6.2 + Nitro Node SSR proof in `/proof/nuxt-ssr/README.md`
reuses the SFC compiler through a local Nuxt module. It verifies SSR without
JavaScript, matching hydration, active-locale lazy components and pages, Nitro API
macros, parallel request isolation, and full-document locale navigation in
English, German, French, and Spanish. Nitro owns the production server catalog
store and embeds browser locale bindings at build time. This root-mounted,
same-origin, query-locale proof remains outside the six-family matrix; no Nuxt
package is published. CDN/subpath assets, other Nitro presets, prerendering,
streaming, islands, catalog HMR, and other locale URL strategies are not verified.

But Palamedes intentionally avoids some historical Lingui surface area:

- no explicit-ID-first public model
- no recommendation to introduce helper macros only to compensate for unclear expressions
- no preference for numeric placeholder fallback authoring
- fewer overlapping runtime paths

Use source strings and optional context as the public identity. If two source strings need distinct translations, use context rather than an arbitrary ID.

Plural authoring supports ICU `offset`, so "X, Y and 3 others" style sentences
do not need hand-rolled arithmetic in application code:

```tsx
plural(count, { offset: 1, "=0": "nobody else", one: "one other", other: "# others" })
```

```tsx
<Plural value={count} offset={1} _0="nobody else" one="one other" other="# others" />
```

The same message written directly in a catalog is `{count, plural, offset:1 =0 {…} one {…} other {# others}}`. Exact `=N` keys match the raw value; plural categories and `#` use the value minus the offset.

Authored source strings may contain apostrophes (`don't`) without escaping — the
macros and the extractor emit ICU-safe patterns automatically. Translators
editing `.po` files by hand use standard ICU quoting: `''` for a literal
apostrophe, and `'{'` to emit a literal brace.

## Placeholder guidance

Good placeholder authoring should be stable and readable for translators.

Prefer:

```tsx
const userName = user.name
const inboxCount = inbox.items.length

return t`Hello ${userName}, you have ${inboxCount} messages`
```

Avoid complex inline expressions that would force numeric fallback placeholders:

```tsx
// Avoid this shape in Palamedes guidance.
return t`Hello ${user.profile?.displayName ?? getFallbackName()}, you have ${inbox.items.length} messages`
```

Instead, extract named variables first. Palamedes should be allowed to reject placeholder shapes that cannot produce stable, meaningful names.

## Runtime model

The public runtime access model is `getI18n()`.

App code creates and activates an i18n instance. Transformed macro code can then resolve the active instance through the runtime bridge. Do not invent separate framework-specific runtime semantics unless the relevant Palamedes adapter documents them.

## Catalog model

Palamedes uses source-string-first `.po` catalogs by default and delegates catalog/ICU semantics to `ferrocat`. Teams can opt into FCL when they want canonical, merge-friendly generated catalogs with cleaner machine-owned metadata (see `/docs/catalog-formats.md`).

Important consequences:

- catalog semantics should not be duplicated in React, Solid, Vite, or Next adapters
- `message + context` is the stable identity users should think about
- generated internal compiled lookup keys are implementation details
- source control diffs should stay reviewable and gettext-adjacent
- catalog health checks should use `pmds audit` or the `auditCatalogs(...)` API
- completeness gates should use `pmds report --fail-if-below <percent>`

### Translation candidate and patch APIs

Custom translation tooling can use the typed APIs from
`@palamedes/core-node`:

```ts
import {
  applyTranslationPatches,
  listTranslationCandidates,
} from "@palamedes/core-node"
```

`listTranslationCandidates(...)` reads configured PO/FCL catalogs and returns
candidates plus diagnostics. A candidate has a stable identity and a
`fingerprint`; carry that fingerprint into `applyTranslationPatches(...)` so a
patch is rejected when the current catalog no longer matches the candidate.
The candidate/patch type surface is `TranslationCandidateId`,
`TranslationCandidate`, `TranslationCandidateRequest`,
`TranslationCandidateResult`, `TranslationPatch`, `TranslationPatchRequest`,
`TranslationPatchOutcomeStatus`, `TranslationPatchOutcome`,
`TranslationPatchResult`, and `TranslationPatchWriteError`. The patch result
reports `applied`, `unchanged`, `rejected`, or `notApplied` outcomes and
diagnostics. Patch validation shares native ICU compatibility rules with
`auditCatalogs(...)`: missing arguments, changed kinds, offsets, required
selectors, rich-text tags, and plain argument occurrence counts are checked
before any catalog write. Compatible target-language plural categories are
allowed. Compatibility errors retain audit's `icu.*` codes and explanations;
audit warnings do not reject patches. A failed catalog replacement throws an error with a partial report;
do not treat a thrown write error as proof that no earlier catalog patch completed.

`checkTranslationTargets({ targets: patches, checks: { boundaryWhitespace: true,
metadataLeakage: true } })` checks proposed `TranslationValue` content without
catalog I/O. Both checks default to disabled. `auditCatalogs(config, { checks:
{ targetText: { boundaryWhitespace: true, metadataLeakage: true } } })` uses the
same native detector on stored PO/FCL values. `target.boundary_whitespace` warns
about introduced whole-message boundary whitespace, exempting source boundaries
with intentional whitespace. Internal ICU branch/rich-text spacing and NBSP
before punctuation are unchanged. `target.metadata_leakage` warns about additional
native PO `#@ key:` markers in visible ICU literals; source exemptions match each
key and occurrence count. No global language or address blacklist is applied.
Preflight returns one `TranslationTargetTextResult` per input with warnings:
shared candidate `id`, checked `target`, and `diagnostics`. Each diagnostic has
severity `warning` and a half-open UTF-8 byte `span` into its result's `target`
(original singular or natively rendered plural ICU). Payload and identity occur
once per input, and inputs without warnings are omitted. Audit spans index the decoded stored target, not file text. Invalid
ICU remains the existing syntax validator's concern; malformed projected plural
branches can fail native rendering, while malformed singular strings are skipped.
These advisory checks never
write, trim, clear review markers, or reject patches.

`inspectCatalogMachineTranslations(config, { locales? })` inspects PO/FCL machine
claims without rewriting files. Its `catalogs` sections identify the catalog
pattern, target path, and locale, with active-entry `current`, `stale`, `absent`,
and `invalid` counters and `details` rows (`message`, optional `context`, `status`).
Ferrocat owns all hash and status rules. Obsolete entries are excluded; missing
source/target catalogs and parse failures reject the call. Malformed metadata may
be rejected or discarded before review, so invalid is not a complete detector.
Integrity establishes neither authorship nor linguistic quality. This is separate
from candidate concurrency fingerprints and leaves extraction cleanup unchanged.
`inspectCatalogMachineTranslationsAsync(config, options?, taskOptions?)` has the
same result/error contract on the shared libuv pool.

File-touching operations also have additive promise-returning variants:
`updateCatalogFileAsync`, `applyTranslationPatchesAsync`,
`compileCatalogArtifactAsync`, `compileCatalogArtifactSelectedAsync`,
`compileCatalogModuleAsync`, and `extractCatalogMessagesFromFilesAsync`.
They preserve the synchronous result and error shapes while scheduling one
owned operation on Node's shared libuv worker pool. The Vite and Next plugin
hooks await them; the Remix synchronous module hook keeps
`compileCatalogModule`. These promises do not cancel queued native work, so
custom bulk callers must bound their own concurrency rather than launch an
unbounded promise fan-out.

Same-key `compileCatalogArtifactSelectedAsync` calls and async mutations of the
same resolved catalog are coordinated within one loaded JavaScript module
instance. Loading both the CommonJS and ESM entry points, or multiple package
copies, creates independent build coordinators and mutation queues. The
synchronous selected compiler bypasses JavaScript coordination and can block
the Node.js event loop while it waits for an in-flight native build. Separate
module instances and processes, plus concurrent synchronous mutations, require
caller coordination.

## CLI model

The native CLI loads English, German, Spanish, and French UI translations compiled from
its PO catalogs into external `<locale>.pmd.json` files. No language, including
English, is embedded. It selects the first nonempty value in
`PALAMEDES_UI_LOCALE > LC_ALL > LC_MESSAGES > LANG` order. POSIX encodings and
modifiers are stripped; supported base languages handle regional tags. Invalid,
unsupported, C/POSIX, and absent values select English without falling through
to a lower-priority variable. This controls UI output independently of catalog
`--locale` filters. JSON documents, raw values, diagnostic codes, and exit codes
stay stable. Compiler/OS/third-party details, Clap argument-error details, and
plugin-owned messages retain their wording. Node is not needed at runtime.
Platform packages install catalogs in `bin/pmds-locales/` beside the executable;
`PALAMEDES_UI_CATALOG_DIR` can override the directory. Only the selected locale is
loaded. Missing/corrupt/incompatible catalogs fail before execution without
another-language or source-text recovery. See `docs/cli.md#output-language`.

Experimental, unpublished workspace crates `palamedes-build` and `palamedes-i18n`
expose the Rust application path. A Cargo build script uses `CatalogBuilder` to
write generated `macro_rules!` definitions/schema and external catalogs. Rustc
expands source-first calls through one sorted const table and binary search into
internal-ID lookups. Each call expands a small lookup, not the whole catalog.
A source-free `schema.pmd.json` exports the immutable message contract. The runtime decodes compiled
instructions without PO/ICU parsing, supports independent explicit locale
contexts, and validates version, locale, inventory, arguments, and contract
fingerprint. Literal text, display arguments, string selects, and cardinal/ordinal
plurals are supported. Plural rules use cached ICU4X/CLDR data for the catalog's
locale, including regional distinctions. Exact numeric branches precede category
selection; offset-adjusted counts drive categories and `#`. Nested plural/select
scopes and quoted pound signs retain ICU semantics. `#` emits plain decimal text;
localized number/date/time formatting, rich text, and contexts fail compilation.
Generated signatures require built-in integer/float types or a validated
PluralNumber for plural/ordinal arguments; bare strings and other Display values
fail Rust compilation in those positions. Nonplural arguments retain Display.
Parse decimal strings into PluralNumber to preserve visible fractional zeros.
Translations and updates cannot turn a display-only source argument into a plural.
Plural values render as signed plain decimals, at most 18 fractional digits with
an i128 coefficient (also after offset subtraction).
Invalid/non-finite/exponent values and overflow return Error::PluralArgument;
visible fractional zeros matter to CLDR. Rule payloads keep Catalog Send + Sync.
Instruction format version 2 requires regenerating version 1 catalogs and schemas
with the matching executable once before independent translation updates.
`extract_messages()` provides token-based Rust source extraction; the CLI's
existing extraction command has not gained a Rust frontend. Build-time missing
or fuzzy translations resolve through the configured fallback chain and source
locale/message, with diagnostics; `.fail_on_missing(true)` is opt-in, enabled
explicitly for the CLI UI. Runtime delivery errors never render fallback text.
`pmds catalog compile --target rust --schema <schema.pmd.json> --catalog-dir <dir>
--locale <tag> --output <dir>` compiles real PO updates against the exported schema
without invoking Cargo or rustc for the application. Repeat `--locale` and
`--fallback-locale`; `--fail-on-missing` rejects incomplete translations; `--json`
returns `catalogs` paths and `missing` records (`locale`, `message`, `resolvedLocale`).
All compatibility checks finish before writes; selected files are atomically
replaced and other installed locales are preserved. `Catalog::load` preserves
paths for all failures and distinguishes format, locale, and fingerprint errors.
The CLI's fixed English bootstrap error names the UI locale, attempted locations,
cause, and reinstall/PALAMEDES_UI_CATALOG_DIR repair. Native packaging uses Cargo
JSON artifact and OUT_DIR paths, not an assumed target/profile layout.
For source checkouts, bootstrap diagnostics explain that cargo run does not
refresh old target/profile sidecars: rebuild the native platform package or point
PALAMEDES_UI_CATALOG_DIR at the current CLI build-script out_dir/catalogs reported
by cargo build -p palamedes-cli --message-format=json. Human fallback warnings
quote source messages like build.rs; JSON keeps the raw message text.
The crates.io hold
remains in force. See `docs/rust-applications.md` and `crates/palamedes-i18n/examples/cli`.
The Preview Rust SDK stays in the coordinated version set and is not published on crates.io. `pnpm verify:rust-sdk` checks actual Cargo archives, rustdoc, a staged-registry version-only consumer, and an unchanged binary after a native CLI translation update. `pnpm release:rust:dry-run` uploads nothing; the Cargo lane requires both policy and manifest publication guards to be explicitly enabled in an authorized release change.

Unbundled Node code (native type stripping, plain `tsc` output, scripts, tests)
can keep the `t`, `plural`, `select`, and `selectOrdinal` macros from
`@palamedes/core/macro`: `pmds extract --runtime-manifest .palamedes/macros.json`
records each call's static text, compiled key, and placeholder names, and
`pmds catalog compile --target js --output .palamedes/catalogs` writes one
parser-free `<locale>.mjs` per locale. Call `registerRuntimeMacros(url)` from
`@palamedes/runtime/node-macros` once at startup and `i18n.load(locale, messages)`
from the compiled module. Unregistered macros keep throwing; unknown calls and
missing catalogs throw instead of rendering source text. Runtime collisions and
interpolated choice branches are extraction errors. Bundled code compiles
macros with a plugin instead; Node load hooks, `tsc` preprocessing, and JSX
macros are unsupported here. `defineNodeI18n({ generated })` from
`@palamedes/runtime/node` wraps both steps, and server builds with
`@palamedes/vite-plugin` resolve it to the bundled catalog store, so one module
serves bundled and unbundled backends. See `docs/backend-servers.md`.

Core commands:

```bash
pnpm exec pmds extract
pnpm exec pmds lint
pnpm exec pmds audit
pnpm exec pmds report
```

Useful options include:

```bash
pnpm exec pmds extract --clean
pnpm exec pmds extract --check --json
pnpm exec pmds extract --fail-on-empty-catalog
pnpm exec pmds extract --watch
pnpm exec pmds extract --verbose
pnpm exec pmds extract --runtime-manifest .palamedes/macros.json
pnpm exec pmds catalog compile --target js --output .palamedes/catalogs
pnpm exec pmds lint --json
pnpm exec pmds lint --fail-on warning
pnpm exec pmds lint src/view.tsx src/actions.ts --json --fail-on warning
pnpm exec pmds audit --json
pnpm exec pmds audit --fail-on warning
pnpm exec pmds report --json
pnpm exec pmds report --fail-if-below 90
```

`extract`, `lint`, `audit`, `report`, `catalog merge`, `catalog merge-driver`,
and `catalog convert` accept `--config <path>` where configuration is relevant.
Use `pmds extract --force-clean` to remove every obsolete entry. `audit` and
`report` accept `--locale <locale...>`. `catalog merge`, `catalog merge-driver`,
and `catalog convert` accept `--source-locale <locale>` and `--locale <locale>`
for catalog semantics.

`pmds lint` is non-mutating source-authoring validation for the configured
source files (including MDX, Vue scripts, and Svelte scripts). Explicit file
arguments replace discovery, resolve relative to the invocation directory, and
bypass catalog include/exclude patterns while retaining project lint policy.
Use literal files, not directories or quoted globs. Missing, unreadable, or
unsupported inputs appear in `failedFiles` and exit with code `4`. It has human
or deterministic JSON output; `--fail-on warning` also makes warnings fail. Its
cache is shared with extraction, and targeted runs preserve other cached files;
use `--no-cache` when the run must not write the cache. Agents should lint changed
files after edits, run `pmds extract --check --json --fail-on-empty-catalog` for
catalog drift after extraction, and use `pmds audit --json --fail-on warning` for
catalog translation and ICU checks. A targeted lint pass is not a full-project
or catalog validation.
An extraction-cache write failure does not change the command verdict, but it
always emits a stderr warning even without `--verbose`. Watch mode reports a
persistent write failure once per process rather than once per file event. Use
`--no-cache` or `extract-cache: false` for intentionally unwritable cache
locations.

`pmds extract --check --json` projects the configured PO/FCL catalogs through
the normal extraction and serialization path, compares the result with disk,
and reports deterministic clean, drift, or error data. It exits nonzero for
drift without writing catalog files or creating missing catalog directories.
The extraction cache may still be updated unless `--no-cache` is passed.

`--fail-on-empty-catalog` turns a catalog that matches no source files into an
operational failure before any configured catalog is written or marked
obsolete. Without the flag, extraction keeps the warning-only behavior and
projects that catalog from an empty message set. With `--check --json`, the
guarded failure uses status `error`, an empty `catalogs` array, and exit code
`1`. Watch mode reports the failed cycle, leaves catalogs unchanged, and keeps
watching for a source change that can recover.

### CLI exit codes

| Code | CI meaning |
| ---- | ---------- |
| `0` | The command completed and its configured policy passed. |
| `1` | Configuration, I/O, serialization, or another operational failure prevented completion. |
| `2` | Invalid command-line usage rejected by Clap. |
| `3` | `extract --check` completed and found catalog drift. |
| `4` | `lint` completed and its `--fail-on` policy failed, or source analysis failed for one or more files. |
| `5` | `audit` completed and its `--fail-on` policy failed. |
| `6` | `report` completed and one or more locales were below `--fail-if-below`. |

Catalog utilities:

```bash
pnpm exec pmds catalog merge --conflict-strategy=use-first --output out.po a.po b.po
pnpm exec pmds catalog merge-driver %O %A %B %A --path %P --conflict-strategy=use-first
pnpm exec pmds catalog convert --to fcl input.po
```

`catalog merge` takes exactly two input files. Add `--base base.po` for a
deletion-aware three-way merge. Supported PO/FCL extensions infer the format;
set `--format po` or `--format fcl` only to explicitly override that
inference. For Git, use `catalog merge-driver` rather than reconstructing Git
role mapping in a wrapper:

```bash
git config merge.palamedes-catalog.driver \
  'pmds catalog merge-driver %O %A %B %A --path %P --conflict-strategy=use-first'
```

The merge driver receives ancestor, current, other, and output positional paths
from Git and needs `--path %P` to apply configured catalog formatting and infer
PO or FCL from the logical path when Git temporary paths are extensionless.
This one driver supports mixed-format repositories; set `--format po` or
`--format fcl` only as an explicit override. It detects rebases and swaps
Git's temporary roles so `use-first` consistently means the branch being
merged or rebased. Use `--operation merge` or `--operation rebase` only for
unusual Git orchestration.

Extraction performance is already handled by the CLI and needs no user tuning by default. `pmds extract` runs a bounded parallel read/parse pass (`--threads <COUNT>`, or `extract-threads` in the config) and reuses an on-disk extraction cache (`--no-cache` disables it for one run; `extract-cache: false` disables it permanently).

The thread default is `4`, clamped to the available cores and the number of files; `1` runs serial. It is a measured floor, not a core count: a one-shot `pmds extract` pays worker setup on every invocation and gets slower again above it. Do not recommend raising `--threads` without a measurement on the user's own corpus and hardware. Both keys are read by the native CLI only — the JS config loader in `@palamedes/config` ignores them. See `/adr/023-bounded-parallel-extraction.md` and `/adr/022-extraction-cache.md`.

Plugin commands:

```bash
pnpm exec pmds <plugin> <command> [...args]
```

Third-party CLI plugins must be explicitly listed under `plugins` in the
Palamedes configuration — installed packages are never auto-discovered.
Plugins are binary-only native executables that implement the versioned binary
plugin protocol. The host caches validated manifests under `.palamedes` by
canonical binary path and file metadata, re-describes them when the binary,
host, or protocol identity changes, and treats cache failures as non-fatal.
See `/docs/cli.md`, `/docs/api/cli-binary-plugin.md`,
`/adr/015-cli-plugin-execution-boundary.md`, and
`/adr/025-binary-plugin-protocol.md`.

## Framework guidance

Package roots and existing `compiled` aliases use one parser-free v2 runtime.
Missing compiled entries throw `MissingCompiledMessageError`; execution failures
also propagate to host error handling. `onMissing`/`onError` are observers, not
fallback handlers. `includeSourceMetadata` retains diagnostic source metadata
only; it cannot restore source rendering. Its v1 name `keepSourceFallbacks`
throws a migration error. Missing
translations instead use the compiler's fallback chain. Its v2 default is
`false` (v1 adapters defaulted to `true`), which omits that diagnostic metadata
and keeps output compact. Standard adapters provide adapter-owned
active-locale compiled delivery, shared server catalog storage and ordinary host error UI;
applications do not serialize raw ICU or maintain catalog maps. See
`/docs/migration-v2.md`.

The Vite, Next.js, and Remix adapters share one path contract. `projectRoot`
is the base for config discovery, a relative `configPath`, and relative
`include`/`exclude` globs; Vite defaults it to its resolved `root`. The v1
`cwd` option throws a migration error. `include`/`exclude` accept a glob, a
RegExp, or an array of both; RegExps test the absolute file path. See
`/docs/configuration.md#adapter-paths`.

### Vite

Use `@palamedes/vite-plugin`. Put `palamedes()` in the Vite plugin list alongside the host framework plugin.

### Next.js

Use `@palamedes/next-plugin`. Keep Next-specific behavior in the adapter; do
not move catalog semantics into application code. Client messages follow the
Next module graph automatically; do not set the removed `messageSplitting`
option, which throws a migration error with any value. Request-local i18n for
recognized Server Functions and Actions is enabled automatically when exactly
one `palamedes.server` module exists in the project root or `src`; it must
export `initializeServerFunctionI18n`. `serverFunctions: false` opts out;
`serverFunctions: true` makes a missing module a configuration error. The
initializer should load and activate a fresh request-local instance and be
request-memoized or idempotent.

Keep locale negotiation read-only. Do not write or renew locale cookies in the
Server Function initializer or on every Server Action POST in middleware/proxy;
even an unchanged cookie write can render the page again and invalidate
prefetched routes. Resolve missing or unsupported cookies through fallback
without persisting them during a read-only action. Persist explicit locale
choices separately and skip unchanged writes. Application data mutations own
their revalidation or `router.refresh()` calls. Locale changes navigate to a new
document after persistence; global layout revalidation is not needed solely
for that navigation, though cookie mutation can still trigger an action render.

### Remix v3

Use `@palamedes/remix`. Register it after `remix/node-tsx`. Share one
`createPalamedesRemixCatalogAssetRegistry()` between the browser asset loader
and `createRemixI18nServer({ catalogAssets: { registry } })`. Server locale
catalogs load lazily and are shared immutably. Render `renderClientCatalog(locale)`
and `await renderClientEntry(entryPath, { assetServer })`; the adapter emits the
stable asset-server import map for the application and bootstrap (pass `nonce`
with a restrictive script CSP); serve registry and server catalog handlers
before the Remix asset server. The adapter owns readiness, selected executable
browser fragments and ordinary error-page recovery. Apps own locale selection
and optional untranslated error markup. Inert ICU bootstrap payloads are rejected.
Locale changes reload the document; only the active locale is requested. For matching
date/time output during hydration, set `data-palamedes-time-zone="Europe/Berlin"`
on `<html>` and use `createI18n: () => createI18n({ timeZone: "Europe/Berlin" })`
for the server instance. The adapter reads the document zone before browser modules run.
Development watches catalog/config inputs; custom runners can use `watch: true`
or `registry.invalidate()`. Node.js >=24.3 and remix@3.0.0 are the verified
host. All four locale strategies have browser proofs, including Frames, interaction,
reloads, and initial/lazy catalog recovery under CSP. External verification uses
`pnpm verify:examples:browser -- --id remix-<strategy> --base-url <HTTPS-origin>`;
see /docs/api/remix.md and /docs/demo-deployments.md for public hosts and hosting evidence.


### React Router RSC

Use `@palamedes/react-router-rsc` only for the exact tested experimental React Router RSC Framework Mode contract. Configure a custom `app/entry.rsc.tsx` that wraps the default RSC entry with `createReactRouterRscI18nRequestScope(createRequestI18n)`. It receives the original request and activates a fresh i18n instance before Server Function argument evaluation, dispatch, revalidation, SSR, and streams. `scope.run()` restores its caller after dispatch settles, but async resources created inside it retain the request locale when they run later; separately initiated work without an inherited context has no active locale and needs explicit data or a new scope. RSC Data Mode, Edge/Worker runtimes, and graph-split server message fragments are not supported. See `/docs/api/react-router-rsc.md`.

### Waku support status

Waku support is Preview, verified with Waku 1.0.0-rc.3 and React/React DOM/react-server-dom-webpack 19.3.1 on Node.js >=22.22.0. Upstream Waku is an RC. Required unstable_getRequest and host CSP unstable_setNonce APIs keep the adapter outside the Stable SemVer contract independently of the unreleased Palamedes v2 publication preview. Re-evaluate after stable equivalents exist and request/action/stream/catalog recovery/CSP proofs pass; stable upstream 1.0 alone does not promote it. See /docs/stability.md#waku-preview-contract and /docs/api/waku.md.

### TanStack Start, Solid, Waku, React Router

Use the verified examples as the source of truth for framework-specific wiring. Palamedes' goal is a consistent runtime/catalog model across these hosts.

React Router Framework Mode has no adapter package: it uses `@palamedes/vite-plugin` plus application-owned server wiring (request-scoped server i18n, the catalog document transform in `app/entry.server.tsx`, and scoped loaders and actions). See `/docs/api/react-router.md`.

## Migration from Lingui-shaped code

When migrating Lingui-style code:

- keep macro-style authoring where it maps cleanly
- move away from explicit IDs as a public habit
- prefer `message + context`
- avoid carrying deprecated Lingui configuration or macro package patterns forward
- keep runtime setup explicit and aligned with Palamedes' runtime bridge
- validate catalog output with `pmds extract` and `pmds audit`

## What not to add casually

Avoid adding these unless a Palamedes issue/ADR explicitly expands scope:

- Vue extractor behavior
- React Native/Metro integration
- Astro/Svelte integration
- generic Lingui compatibility layers
- explicit message ID migration as a primary product path
- unbounded CLI fan-out (one worker per core) or raised `--threads` defaults without benchmark evidence
- new placeholder macros that merely work around unclear variable names

## Development commands

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm test
pnpm check-types
pnpm verify:examples
```

Some local environments may lack Rust/Cargo for native rebuilds. In that case, prefer documentation-only checks and targeted package checks, and let CI validate full native builds.

CLI usage reporting controls: `pmds telemetry enable --accept telemetry-v1`,
`pmds telemetry status`, `pmds telemetry preview`, `pmds telemetry disable`,
`pmds telemetry decline`, `pmds telemetry delete`, `pmds telemetry flush`,
`pmds telemetry reset`, and
`pmds telemetry forget --acknowledge-unverified-deletion`. `--offline` is a
global CLI flag that prevents update/telemetry networking. `enable` without
`--accept` only displays the notice. No automatic consent prompt is shown.
